Furthermore, the pseudo-second-order model successfully described the variations in total Cr biosorption capacity at the different initial Cr(VI) concentrations and temperatures assayed (continuous lines in Figs 3 and 5), and predicted values of biosorption capacity at equilibrium very close to the equilibrium capacities obtained experimentally (Tables 1 and 2). Incidentally, the pseudo-second-order model had been previously found to be the most suitable model to describe the kinetic profiles of total Cr biosorption by CLB at different solution pH levels [27]. The fitness of total Cr biosorption kinetics to the pseudo-second-order model suggests that the rate-limiting step in biosorption of Cr ions onto CLB is probably a chemical sorption (chemisorption) involving valence forces through the sharing or exchange of electrons between the CLB surface and Cr ions [38].
